blocks.text: Stephen Corporate Services (SCS) Ltd ("SCS", "we", "us" or "our") uses cookies and similar technologies to operate, protect, and improve its websites and online services.
This Cookie Policy explains the technologies we use, the purposes for which they are used, how they may process information about visitors, and how you can control your preferences.

We distinguish between cookies that are necessary for our websites to function and those used for additional purposes, such as analytics, personalisation, and marketing. We do not activate non-essential cookies unless you have given the required consent.
This Policy forms part of our Privacy Notice and should be read alongside it. It applies to SCS websites, online services, and client portals that display or link to this Policy.

We administer cookies and similar technologies in accordance with the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, the applicable provisions of the Nigeria Data Protection Act General Application and Implementation Directive 2025 (GAID), and other relevant legal requirements.

sections.heading: 2. Who Is Responsible for Our Use of Cookies?

blocks.text: Stephen Corporate Services (SCS) Ltd is responsible for determining how cookies and similar technologies are used on the websites and online services covered by this Policy, subject to the respective roles and obligations of third-party service providers.
If you have questions about our use of cookies, wish to exercise your privacy rights, or need assistance with your cookie preferences, you may contact us using the details above.

sections.heading: 3. What Are Cookies and Similar Technologies?

blocks.text: Cookies are small text files that a website stores on your device when you visit it. They may help the website remember your session, maintain security, retain preferences, or recognise a returning browser.
Cookies may be temporary or persistent:

items: **Session cookies** generally expire when you close your browser or when the relevant session ends.
**Persistent cookies** remain on your device for a defined period or until you delete them.

blocks.text: We may also use technologies that perform functions similar to cookies. These include tracking pixels, web beacons, browser storage, scripts, and other mechanisms that recognise a device, store information, or collect information about interactions with a website.
For the purposes of this Policy, references to cookies include these similar technologies where applicable.

Depending on the technology and its purpose, information collected may include your browser or device information, IP address, session identifiers, pages visited, interactions with website features, and cookie preferences.
Such information may constitute personal data where it relates to an identified or identifiable individual.

We classify cookies according to their purpose. The categories below describe the functions that may be used on our websites and online services. The actual cookies deployed must correspond to the categories disclosed in our cookie preference interface.
These cookies support essential website functions and security.
They may be used to:

items: Maintain secure browsing sessions.
Support authentication and access to protected client portals.
Protect website forms and sessions against unauthorised activity.
Support network stability and the reliable delivery of website content.
Maintain essential accessibility features.
Remember your cookie consent or rejection choices.

blocks.text: We use these cookies only where they are necessary for the relevant function. They are not used as a means of introducing unrelated advertising or behavioural tracking.
Strictly necessary cookies that fall within the applicable legal exemption do not require consent. Their use remains subject to applicable data protection principles and other legal obligations.
These cookies help us understand how visitors use our websites and whether our online services are functioning properly.
Depending on the tools deployed, they may help us:

items: Understand which pages receive visits.
Identify broken links and error pages.
Measure page-loading times.
Assess the performance and usability of website features.
Identify general usage patterns that can guide improvements.

blocks.text: Where these functions involve non-essential cookies or similar tracking technologies, we obtain your consent before activating them.
Analytics cookies remain disabled if you reject them. We do not treat the fact that you visit our website as permission to use these technologies.
These cookies enable additional features and help us remember choices you make while using our websites.
Depending on the functionality provided, they may remember your language preference, interface settings, or other selected options.
Where a cookie is not strictly necessary for a function you have requested, we seek your consent before using it.

If you reject functional cookies, some optional features may not remember your preferences between visits. The essential functions of the website should remain available where technically practicable.
These cookies and similar technologies may be used to measure marketing campaigns, understand engagement with promotional content, or support the delivery of relevant advertising.
Depending on the service involved, they may recognise a browser across visits or collect information about interactions with marketing content.
We do not activate marketing cookies or equivalent non-essential tracking technologies without your consent.
If we do not use these technologies on a particular website or service, we will not deploy them merely because this category appears in this Policy.
We do not use cookies as a means of selling your personal data.

sections.heading: 5. How We Obtain and Manage Your Consent

blocks.text: When you first visit a website covered by this Policy, our cookie preference interface should provide clear information about our use of cookies and allow you to make an informed choice.
The interface is designed to operate as follows:
**a. Clear notice:** The cookie notice identifies SCS and explains why cookies are used.
**b. Meaningful choice:** You can accept or reject non-essential cookies without being required to accept them to access the website's ordinary functions.
**c. Category selection:** Where different categories of non-essential cookies are available, you can manage them separately through the preference settings.
**d. No preselected consent:** Non-essential categories are not enabled by default, and consent is not inferred from silence, continued browsing, or failure to close the notice.
**e. Essential functionality:** Strictly necessary cookies may operate without consent where the applicable legal exemption permits their use.
**f. Recorded preferences:** We maintain an appropriate record of your choice so that your preferences can be respected and, where necessary, demonstrated.
**g. Continued control:** You can revisit your preferences and withdraw consent as explained in Section 8.

We seek consent before activating non-essential cookies. If you reject a category, the relevant cookies and tracking technologies must remain disabled unless another lawful basis and applicable legal requirement permit the specific processing.
Our consent mechanism should respect your choice throughout the relevant browsing experience and should not repeatedly ask you to make the same choice without a legitimate reason.
The cookies used on a website may change when we introduce new features, update our systems, or change service providers.
For this reason, the cookie preference interface should provide an up-to-date inventory of the cookies and similar technologies actually deployed on the relevant website.
For each applicable cookie or technology, the inventory should identify:

items: Its name and provider.
The category to which it belongs.
Its purpose.
Whether it is a session or persistent cookie.
Its applicable expiry period.
Whether it involves a third party.
The relevant consent requirement.

blocks.text: We do not represent that every category described in this Policy is necessarily active on every SCS website or client portal.
Cookie information must reflect the technologies actually in use, rather than assumed names, providers, or expiry periods.
Session cookies should expire when their intended session ends, unless a documented technical requirement justifies a different period.

Persistent cookies should remain active only for the period reasonably required for their stated purpose. Their expiry periods should be disclosed through the cookie inventory or preference interface.

We retain cookie preference records for the period reasonably necessary to respect your choices and demonstrate that consent was obtained where required. We then delete or appropriately anonymise those records when they are no longer needed, subject to applicable legal obligations.

Where cookie-related information is retained in security logs, analytics systems, or other records, its retention is governed by the relevant purpose, our retention arrangements, and applicable legal requirements.
Some website functions may depend on external service providers, such as hosting providers, security services, analytics platforms, embedded media providers, or other technology vendors.
Depending on how a service is configured, a provider may store cookies on your device or receive information through similar technologies.
We assess the technologies incorporated into our websites and take reasonable steps to understand:

items: What information the provider collects.
Why the information is collected.
Whether the provider uses cookies or similar tracking technologies.
Whether personal data is disclosed to the provider.
Whether information is transferred outside Nigeria.
What contractual, technical, and organisational safeguards are appropriate.

blocks.text: Where a third-party technology requires consent, we obtain that consent before activating it.

Third-party providers may operate under their own privacy policies and contractual terms. Where appropriate, we direct you to the relevant provider's privacy information through our cookie preference interface.
The involvement of a third party does not remove SCS's responsibility to assess and manage its own data protection obligations.

sections.heading: 8. Changing Your Preferences and Withdrawing Consent

blocks.text: You may change your cookie preferences or withdraw consent at any time.
Use the **Cookie Settings** option on the relevant website to reopen the preference interface.
You can use this interface to withdraw consent for previously accepted categories or change your selections.
Withdrawal must be made available through a straightforward mechanism and must not be unnecessarily more difficult than giving consent.
Once your preference changes, we will take reasonable technical steps to stop using the affected non-essential cookies and tracking technologies.

Some cookies may already have been stored on your device. We will provide a mechanism to delete or disable them where technically practicable. You may also need to remove existing cookies through your browser settings.

Withdrawing consent does not invalidate processing that was lawfully carried out before withdrawal. It does, however, require us to stop relying on that consent for subsequent processing to which the withdrawal applies.
Most modern browsers allow you to view, delete, block, or restrict cookies.
You may also configure your browser to restrict third-party cookies or clear selected cookies when you close it.
Instructions are available from the browser providers:

items: Google Chrome: [https://support.google.com/chrome/answer/95647](https://support.google.com/chrome/answer/95647)
Mozilla Firefox: [https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/enhanced-tracking-protection-firefox-desktop](https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/enhanced-tracking-protection-firefox-desktop)
Microsoft Edge: [https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge)
Apple Safari: [https://support.apple.com/guide/safari/sfri11471/mac](https://support.apple.com/guide/safari/sfri11471/mac)

blocks.text: Browser settings operate independently of our website's preference interface. Blocking all cookies may prevent some essential features, including authentication or access to secure client portals, from functioning correctly.
Where you have withdrawn consent through our website, changing your browser settings is not a substitute for the website's responsibility to respect your recorded preference.

sections.heading: 9. Security and Protection of Cookie-Related Information

blocks.text: We take reasonable technical and organisational measures to protect information collected through cookies and similar technologies against unauthorised access, disclosure, alteration, loss, or misuse.

Depending on the relevant system and risk, these measures may include access controls, secure configuration, restricted administrative privileges, appropriate encryption, monitoring, and the use of trusted service providers.
We seek to ensure that cookie-related information is accessed only by persons and systems authorised to use it for legitimate purposes.
We also take reasonable steps to ensure that cookie preference records are handled consistently with the choices made by website visitors.
The safeguards applied to a particular system depend on the information processed, the technology involved, and the risks associated with its use.
Some third-party service providers may process or store cookie-related information outside Nigeria.
Where this occurs, we assess the relevant processing arrangements and apply the international data transfer requirements of the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 and the applicable GAID provisions.
Depending on the circumstances, this may require an assessment of the destination, the recipient, applicable legal safeguards, and the rights and protections available to affected individuals.
We do not treat your acceptance of analytics or marketing cookies as automatic authorisation for every international transfer associated with a provider.
Where consent is relied upon for a particular processing activity or transfer, it must satisfy the applicable legal requirements and relate to the processing in question.
Where information collected through cookies constitutes personal data, you may exercise the rights available to you under applicable data protection law.
Depending on the circumstances, these rights may include:

items: Requesting access to your personal data.
Requesting correction of inaccurate or incomplete information.
Requesting erasure where the applicable conditions are met.
Objecting to certain processing activities.
Withdrawing consent where processing relies on consent.
Lodging a complaint with the relevant supervisory authority.

blocks.text: The availability and application of particular rights depend on the nature of the processing and the applicable legal requirements.
To exercise a right or raise a concern about our use of cookies, contact us using the details in Section 13.
We will assess and respond to your request in accordance with applicable law.
We may revise this Policy when our websites, technologies, service providers, business operations, or applicable legal requirements change.
The latest version will be published on the relevant website with its effective date.
Where a material change affects the way we use non-essential cookies, we will update the relevant disclosures and obtain fresh consent where required before activating the affected technologies.
We will not rely on the publication of an updated Policy as a substitute for obtaining consent where consent is legally required.
We encourage you to review this Policy periodically.

If you have questions about this Policy, wish to change your cookie preferences, or want to raise a concern about our use of cookies, you may contact Stephen Corporate Services (SCS) Ltd through the following channels:
If you are dissatisfied with our handling of a privacy concern, you may lodge a complaint with the Nigeria Data Protection Commission through its official website:
[https://ndpc.gov.ng/](https://ndpc.gov.ng/)
You may also seek any other remedy available to you under applicable law.
